=You are a Senior Agile Product Owner. Analyze the provided Business Requirement
Document (BRD) and decompose it into a technical backlog that will be effort-
estimated by a panel of engineers.

## Requirements

1. EXTRACTION — Identify every distinct functional requirement in the BRD.
   Extract only what the BRD states or directly implies. Do not invent scope.
   If the BRD is silent on something important, that belongs in the story's
   acceptance criteria as an open question, not as a fabricated requirement.

2. STANDARDIZATION — Rewrite each requirement as a Canonical User Story:
   "As a [User Role], I want [Action/Feature], so that [Value/Benefit]."

3. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — Give each story 2-5 concrete, checkable criteria.
   This is what makes a story estimable. "The user can reset their password"
   is not estimable; "the reset link expires after a set period" is.

4. SIZING — Each story must be small enough for one team to complete in a
   single sprint. If a requirement is larger than that, split it into several
   stories. A story nobody can size teaches you nothing.

5. DOMAIN TAGGING — Assign exactly one primary domain per story, drawn only
   from this list:
   Frontend, Backend, Security, Database, DevOps, AI/ML, Integration, Mobile

6. PROJECT CONTEXT — Separately, write 3-6 sentences describing the technical
   environment the work lands in: existing stack, platforms, integrations, and
   constraints stated in the BRD. This is shared background for every story,
   so keep it free of story-specific detail.

## Input

Raw BRD Text: {{ $json.body.summary }}

## Output

Respond ONLY with a single JSON object. No markdown fences, no commentary.

{
  "project_context": "string",
  "stories": [
    {
      "id": "story-01-short-slug",
      "user_story": "As a ..., I want ..., so that ...",
      "acceptance_criteria": ["string", "string"],
      "domain": "string"
    }
  ]
}

The "id" field must be lowercase, hyphenated, ASCII only, numbered in sequence
(story-01-…, story-02-…), and derived from the story's subject. It is used as a
filesystem path and as a join key, so it must be unique and stable.

You are recruiting an expert panel to estimate the effort of a technical product project.

You will receive a Business Requirement Document and the user stories derived
from it. Your job is to decide WHICH KINDS OF ENGINEERS should sit on the
effort estimation panel, then return that decision as JSON.

You are not estimating anything. You are choosing who is qualified to estimate.

## How to choose

Read the BRD and the stories, and identify the technical surfaces the work
actually touches — not the ones the BRD claims. Then select the developer
archetypes whose daily work covers those surfaces.

Apply these rules:

- Select between 3 and 6 archetypes. Fewer than 3 gives you no disagreement
  to learn from; more than 6 dilutes the panel with people who cannot judge
  the work.
- Always include the archetype that owns the dominant technical surface.
- Include "Security engineer" if the work touches authentication, payments,
  personal data, permissions, or regulated information.
- Include "DevOps / SRE / infrastructure" if the work touches deployment,
  environments, pipelines, monitoring, or scaling.
- Include "Engineering manager / lead" whenever there are 5 or more stories —
  someone must judge sequencing and coordination cost.
- Do NOT include an archetype merely because the technology is mentioned in
  passing. A single email notification does not require a Back-end developer
  if the story is otherwise front-end work.

## Allowed values — copy these EXACTLY

dev_role_archetype must be drawn only from this list. Do not invent values,
do not reword them.

  "Front-end developer"
  "Back-end developer"
  "Full-stack developer"
  "Mobile developer"
  "Data / ML developer"
  "DevOps / SRE / infrastructure"
  "Security engineer"
  "Game developer"
  "Embedded / systems developer"
  "Engineering manager / lead"
  "Product / UX technical role"

## Panel size

Set sampleSize to roughly 2 people per archetype you selected, between 6 and
12 total. Two per archetype means that when they disagree you can tell a real
difference of opinion from one person's quirk.

## Output

Return ONE JSON object

{
  "dimensionFilters": {
    "dev_role_archetype": ["<selected archetypes>"],
    "dev_professional_status": ["Professional developer"]
  },
  "sampleSize": <integer 6-12>,
  "rationale": "<2-3 sentences: which technical surfaces you found in the
                 stories, and why these archetypes cover them>"
}

"dev_professional_status" is always exactly ["Professional developer"] —
never change it. It keeps hobbyists and inactive developers off the panel.

body.summary: We want to build an AI system called 'Store-Pulse' to help our store managers handle staffing and security more efficiently across our 40 branches. The main goal is to use our existing CCTV camera feeds to analyze how both staff and customers are behaving on the floor. We need the AI to identify every employee and track their 'Customer Engagement Score' by looking at their movements and facial expressions during their shift. If the AI sees an employee looking tired or unhappy, it should automatically move them to a back-office role and update the staffing schedule in real-time. For customers, the system should recognize 'VIP shoppers' as they enter and send their purchase history to the nearest sales associate's phone. Finally, the system needs to flag 'suspicious behavior' to security if it detects someone looking nervous or hiding items under their clothes.

text.project_context: Store-Pulse will be deployed to process live CCTV camera feeds from 40 retail branches using existing camera endpoints. The system must integrate with the stores' existing scheduling system and the customer purchase-history database, and deliver notifications to store staff phones and security endpoints. Real-time processing requirements imply a low-latency streaming pipeline, ML inference services for face recognition, expression and behavior models, and backend services to persist staff/customer metadata and events. Deployments must be branch-configurable so camera-to-location mappings and branch-specific settings can be managed centrally.

stories.user_story: As a System Operator, I want the system to ingest existing CCTV camera feeds from each branch so that video frames are available for real-time analysis.
acceptance_criteria: System can be configured with one or more camera endpoints (RTSP/HTTP) and successfully open the stream for at least one branch in staging.
System emits time-ordered frames and basic metadata (camera_id, branch_id, timestamp) into the downstream processing pipeline.
Connection failures are logged and a configurable retry policy is applied; retry attempts and error logs are observable.
Open question recorded: supported camera protocols, expected frame rates, and network constraints must be confirmed before production rollout.

stories.user_story: As a Store Admin, I want to register branches and map each camera to a branch and physical location so that analytics and alerts are tagged to the correct branch and area.
acceptance_criteria: API exists to create/update/delete branch records and to register camera_id → branch_id → location_label mappings for each camera.
Mappings are retrievable via API and used by the ingestion pipeline to tag incoming frames with branch and location metadata.
It is possible to bulk-import mappings for multiple cameras/branches to support the 40-branch rollout.
Open question recorded: required location granularity (e.g., zone, aisle, register) must be defined by stakeholders.

stories.user_story: As an HR/Admin user, I want to enroll employees into a registry with reference biometric data so that the system can identify employees on camera.
acceptance_criteria: API to create, read, update, delete employee records exists and stores employee_id, role, and enrollment references (e.g., facial embeddings or reference images).
Enrollment process produces and persists a reference embedding and returns an enrollment success response that can be verified with a test match.
Consent and policy fields are present on the employee record; the presence/meaning of these fields is noted as an open question for legal/compliance.
Enrollment records are versioned and updates to a reference replace or archive prior embeddings per a defined audit trail.

stories.user_story: As the AI system, I want to identify employees and returning customers in camera frames so that persons on the floor are attributed to known identities.
acceptance_criteria: Real-time face detector + recognizer returns person detections with bounding_box, predicted_identity (employee_id or customer_id) and a confidence score for each processed frame.
Recognitions include a confidence score and the recognizer exposes a configurable confidence threshold; matches above threshold are emitted as identity events.
Identity events include camera_id, timestamp, and the recognition confidence; recognition latency (detection->identity event) is measurable and instrumented as a metric.
Open question recorded: acceptable recognition accuracy and privacy/consent requirements for face recognition must be clarified before production use.

stories.user_story: As the AI system, I want to track detected people across consecutive frames (and across overlapping cameras where available) so that movement trajectories can be built for behavior analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Tracker assigns persistent track_id to detections and emits track updates (track_id, bounding_box, camera_id, timestamp) for each frame while the person is continuously visible.
When a person exits visibility and re-enters, the system emits a new track_id unless an overlap-based re-association is possible; behavior of re-association is documented and testable.
Track continuity is demonstrable in tests: a single continuous presence in view produces a single track_id for the duration of visibility.
Open question recorded: expected behavior and accuracy for cross-camera re-association (when and how to link tracks across cameras) must be specified by stakeholders.

stories.user_story: As a Store Manager, I want the system to extract movement-based features for each employee so that part of the Customer Engagement Score can be calculated.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline extracts per-employee movement metrics (e.g., time spent in customer zones, number of approaches to customers, proximity events) and outputs them in a standardized JSON schema per time window.
Movement features are timestamped, associated with employee_id and branch_id, and persisted to the feature store or event log.
Feature outputs include provenance metadata (source camera_ids and track_ids) so downstream scoring can attribute features correctly.
Open question recorded: definition of 'customer zone' and the mapping from camera locations to zones must be confirmed.

stories.user_story: As a Store Manager, I want the system to extract facial-expression features for employees so that emotion-based inputs to the Customer Engagement Score are available.
acceptance_criteria: Facial expression inference produces per-frame labels and confidence scores (e.g., attentive, neutral, happy, sad, tired) for each detected face and writes them to the feature store with timestamps and employee_id when recognized.
Expression features are aggregated into time-window summaries (e.g., percent time attentive) and exposed via API for scoring.
Model outputs include confidence scores and are accompanied by metadata about input frame and camera_id for auditing.
Open question recorded: exact class definitions (what constitutes 'tired' or 'unhappy') and acceptable false positive/negative rates must be defined by stakeholders.

stories.user_story: As a Store Manager, I want a service that consumes movement and facial features and produces a Customer Engagement Score per employee so that engagement can be monitored in real-time.
acceptance_criteria: Service ingests movement and facial-expression feature records and emits a timestamped engagement_score (numeric) for each employee along with the contributing feature breakdown.
Engagement scores are available via a query API by employee_id, branch_id, and time range, and are persisted for the length of retention policy.
Score computation parameters (weights) are configurable; the service records which feature inputs contributed to each score for traceability.
Open question recorded: default scoring formula and required SLA for update frequency must be confirmed by stakeholders before production.

stories.user_story: As the AI system, I want to detect when an employee appears tired or unhappy so that automated workflow actions can be triggered.
acceptance_criteria: Emotion detection component emits an event (employee_id, timestamp, flag: tired_or_unhappy, confidence) when model output exceeds a configurable threshold.
Events are deduplicated within a configurable time window to avoid repeated triggers for the same condition.
Events are logged and visible in the audit trail with the source frames and model confidence for manual review.
Open question recorded: whether automatic actions may be taken without manager approval and acceptable sensitivity/specificity must be clarified.

stories.user_story: As Store-Pulse, I want to call the staffing/scheduling system to change an employee's role to a back-office assignment when they are detected tired/unhappy so that the staffing plan is updated in real-time.
acceptance_criteria: When a tired/unhappy event (per story-09) is emitted, the system invokes the scheduling system API with employee_id, current_shift_id, and new_role(back-office) and records the scheduling API response (success/failure).
Successful calls result in a scheduling_change event recorded in the system event log with timestamp, actor (automated), and API response payload.
If scheduling API returns failure, the system retries per a configurable policy and creates an incident/alert if retries exhaust.
Open question recorded: requirement for manager approval or human-in-the-loop before role change must be clarified and implemented if required.

stories.user_story: As the AI system, I want to recognize VIP shoppers at entry so that VIP events can trigger personalized service workflows.
acceptance_criteria: Entry detection produces an 'entry' event for a person crossing an entry camera line and the face recognizer compares against the VIP list, emitting VIP_detected (customer_id, camera_id, timestamp, confidence) when matched.
VIP_detected events include the camera_id and exact timestamp of entry and are written to the event stream for downstream consumers.
Model returns a confidence score and VIP detection uses a configurable threshold; VIP detection events are auditable with reference frames.
Open question recorded: how the VIP list is maintained (who can modify it) and customer consent policy must be confirmed.

stories.user_story: As a Store Associate, I want to receive a VIP shopper's purchase history on my phone when a VIP enters so that I can provide personalized assistance.
acceptance_criteria: On VIP_detected event, the system queries the customer purchase-history database and retrieves the customer's anonymized purchase history payload.
System determines the nearest sales associate to the VIP entry location using current staff locations or camera-to-staff mapping and selects one associate as the recipient; selection logic is logged.
System sends the purchase-history payload to the selected associate's phone via the configured delivery channel (push/SMS/other) and records a delivery receipt or failure.
Open question recorded: delivery channel(s) and data fields allowed in purchase-history payload (PII scope) must be defined by stakeholders and legal/compliance.

stories.user_story: As a Security Analyst, I want the system to detect suspicious behaviors such as nervousness or concealing items so that security can be alerted.
acceptance_criteria: Behavior model emits suspicious_behavior events with category labels (e.g., nervous, concealing), confidence scores, camera_id, and timestamps when thresholds are exceeded.
Each suspicious_behavior event includes supporting evidence: one or more cropped frame images and corresponding track_id(s) for the person-of-interest.
Events are rate-limited and de-duplicated to prevent alert storms; deduplication window is configurable.
Open question recorded: minimum evidence required for an alert and acceptable false-positive rate must be agreed with security/legal teams prior to rollout.

stories.user_story: As the Security System, I want suspicious behavior alerts delivered to security endpoints so that security personnel can respond quickly.
acceptance_criteria: On suspicious_behavior event, the system posts an alert payload (camera snapshot(s), camera_id, branch_id, timestamp, track_id, category, confidence) to a configurable security endpoint (webhook, dashboard API or push channel) and records delivery status.
System requires and logs an acknowledgement or escalation if the configured security endpoint does not acknowledge within a configurable timeout.
Alert payloads are stored in the audit log and associated with the original camera frames to allow post-incident review.
Open question recorded: the preferred delivery channels for security and the on-call/response procedure must be defined by stakeholders.

text.rationale: The work is dominated by ML surfaces (face recognition, tracking, expression/behavior models) so Data / ML developers are required. Persistent metadata, integrations with scheduling and customer DBs, and notification APIs require Back-end developers. Low-latency streaming, branch deployments, and monitoring demand DevOps/SRE expertise. Biometric/PII handling and alerting require a Security engineer. With 14 stories and multiple teams coordinated, an Engineering manager/lead is needed to judge sequencing and integration costs.

System requires and logs an acknowledgement or escalation if the configured security endpoint does not acknowledge within a configurable timeout.
Alert payloads are stored in the audit log and associated with the original camera frames to allow post-incident review.
Open question recorded: the preferred delivery channels for security and the on-call/response procedure must be defined by stakeholders.
json.projectContext: Store-Pulse will be deployed to process live CCTV camera feeds from 40 retail branches using existing camera endpoints. The system must integrate with the stores' existing scheduling system and the customer purchase-history database, and deliver notifications to store staff phones and security endpoints. Real-time processing requirements imply a low-latency streaming pipeline, ML inference services for face recognition, expression and behavior models, and backend services to persist staff/customer metadata and events. Deployments must be branch-configurable so camera-to-location mappings and branch-specific settings can be managed centrally.
